samples.summary: applyMergeBlocks never adopts the next block's remembered heading level, so Enter-at-start followed by Backspace silently loses the bulleted heading — the exact inverse of the new offset-0 split rule
samples.evidence: `splitMovesHeadingMemory` (block-helpers.ts:290) deliberately MOVES the memory to the split-off block when the split is at offset 0: after `doc.splitBlock('b1', 0)` the leading bullet has no `headingLevel` and the trailing bullet holds level 2 (the new test at test/view/list-heading-roundtrip.test.ts:229-247 asserts exactly this). Now press Backspace at offset 0 of that trailing bullet: `Doc.deleteBackward` (document.ts:289) merges prev+current, i.e. `applyMergeBlocks(emptyLeadingBullet, headingBullet)`. `mergeDropsHeadingMemory(emptyLeadingBullet)` is false (its `headingLevel` is already `undefined`), so nothing is "dropped" — but `merged = cloneBlock(block)` only ever keeps the FIRST block's level, and `nextBlock.headingLevel` (2) is discarded with `nextClone`. The merged block holds all of the heading text yet has no memory, so un-bulleting it yields a plain paragraph. Same loss for the plain case "empty bullet above a bulleted heading, Backspace at the start of the heading". The Yorkie path (yorkie-doc-store.ts:2256) shares `applyMergeBlocks` and likewise never writes the attribute, so cache and tree agree on the wrong value. The provenance rule the PR states ("the memory follows the text") requires `merged.headingLevel = nextBlock.headingLevel` when the target contributes no text.

samples.summary: Pasting over the fully-selected text of a bulleted heading drops its heading memory, while typing over the same selection keeps it
samples.evidence: `handlePaste` calls `deleteSelection()` (text-editor.ts:1253) and then `insertBlocks`. If the user selected all of a bulleted heading's text, the destination block is now an empty `list-item` with `headingLevel`, so `dropsHeadingMemory = pastedTextLen > 0 && mergeDropsHeadingMemory(block)` is true at line 3596 and `delete block.headingLevel` runs at 3599 — un-bulleting afterwards gives a paragraph. The typing path does the same `deleteSelection()` then `docInsertText` (handleInput) with no such deletion, so replacing the same text by typing keeps the level. Replacing a block's text is not a merge of foreign provenance (the block is still the one that was bulleted), so the paste branch loses the level for no reason and the two input methods disagree.

samples.summary: Clipboard table sanitizer defaults a missing column width to 100, but columnWidths are fractions of the content width (1/cols) — a recovered table renders 100x too wide
samples.evidence: `for (let c = 0; c < cols; c++) columnWidths.push(asNumber(rawWidths[c]) ?? 100);`. `columnWidths` are ratios: `createTableBlock` uses `Array(cols).fill(1 / cols)` (types.ts:542), `computeTableLayout` does `columnWidths.map((ratio) => ratio * contentWidth)` (view/table-layout.ts:140), `deleteTableColumn` re-normalizes to `1 / count` (document.ts:703), and the DOCX exporter multiplies by `totalTwips` (docx-exporter.ts:304). A payload whose `columnWidths` is absent, short, or non-numeric therefore yields columns 100x the page content width (and absurd DOCX twips). The fallback should be `1 / cols`.

samples.summary: sanitizeTableData can produce a 0-column table, an invariant createTableBlock explicitly refuses
samples.evidence: `const cols = Math.max(...rows.map((r) => r.cells.length));` — a payload of `{rows:[{cells:[]}]}` passes the `rows.length === 0` guard and yields `cols === 0`, so `columnWidths` is `[]`. `createTableBlock` rejects that state outright (`if (rows < 1 || cols < 1) throw`, types.ts:539). Downstream consumers then work with a table that has rows but no columns: `computeTableLayout` produces empty cell rows, and `selection.ts:448` builds a cell range whose `colIndex` end is `-1`. I could not find a concrete crash (the loops are all `c < numCols` bounded), but the sanitizer is the place that is supposed to re-establish model invariants and it lets a structurally impossible table through instead of dropping it.

samples.summary: foldedHeadingLevel discards a real heading destination's own level when a bullet is pasted into it, inconsistently with the list-item destination branch
samples.evidence: `if (destOwnTextLen > 0) return dest.type === 'list-item' ? dest.headingLevel : undefined;` (line 55-57). When the caret sits in a real `heading` block that keeps its own text and the pasted block is a `list-item`, the head/tail block becomes a `list-item` with no remembered level — the destination's surviving heading text loses its heading provenance, while the identical case with a bulleted-heading destination preserves it (the new test at test/view/list-heading-roundtrip.test.ts:566-593 asserts only the list-item destination). Per the helper's own stated rule ("a destination that keeps its own text keeps its *own* memory"), this branch should return `dest.headingLevel` for `dest.type === 'heading'` too.

finding.summary: Clipboard sanitizer drops `colSpan: 0` covered-cell markers, breaking merged tables on internal paste
finding.evidence:
`sanitizeCell` only keeps a span when it is `> 1`:
```
if (colSpan !== undefined && colSpan > 1) cell.colSpan = Math.trunc(colSpan);
```
But `colSpan: 0` is the *covered-cell marker* the layout relies on — `normalizeTableMerges` (model/types.ts:592) writes `cell.colSpan = 0` for every cell an anchor covers (including rowSpan coverage), and `computeTableLayout` (view/table-layout.ts:158-164) skips a cell only when `colSpan === 0`. Before this change the payload's cells were passed through verbatim, so the markers survived a copy/paste.

The cell-range paste path self-heals (`pasteTableCells` calls `normalizeTableMerges`, text-editor.ts:3708/3740), but the whole-table-block paste path does **not**: `insertBlocks` (text-editor.ts:3565-3584) inserts `cloneBlockWithFreshIds(blocks[0])` with no normalization. So copying a table that contains merged cells and pasting it back produces a table whose merges are gone — the previously covered cells render as real cells with their own width, and any anchor keeps `colSpan > 1`, violating the invariant the layout documents it trusts.

verdict.reason: The code is exactly as described. clipboard.ts:238-241 keeps spans only when `> 1`, discarding the `colSpan: 0` covered-cell marker that types.ts:560-573/592 establishes and table-layout.ts:158-164 relies on (`colSpan === 0` is the only merged-placeholder test). The copy side preserves `0` (`cell.colSpan != null` at text-editor.ts:3451 and clipboard.ts:366), and internal paste goes deserializeClipboard (text-editor.ts:1242) -> sanitizeCell -> insertBlocks, whose whole-table branch (text-editor.ts:3565-3584) and multi-block branch (3653-3657) insert via cloneBlockWithFreshIds (block-helpers.ts:154-169, ids only) and Doc.insertBlockAt/insertBlockAfter (document.ts:440-455) with no normalization. normalizeTableMerges is called only on the cell-range paste paths (text-editor.ts:3708, 3740), and grep found no render-time repair, so no guard makes this unreachable. Result: copy/paste of a table containing merged cells loses the merge structure — covered cells render as real cells while anchors still span them, breaking a documented invariant (data loss of merge metadata). Real and blocking under the correctness rubric at major severity.

finding.summary: `columnWidths` fallback of `100` is in the wrong unit — column widths are ratios, not pixels
finding.evidence:
`for (let c = 0; c < cols; c++) columnWidths.push(asNumber(rawWidths[c]) ?? 100);`

`TableData.columnWidths` holds *fractions*: `createTableBlock` fills `Array(cols).fill(1 / cols)` (model/types.ts:542), the DOCX importer divides by `totalWidth` (import/docx-importer.ts:277), and the layout does `columnWidths.map(ratio => ratio * contentWidth)` (view/table-layout.ts:140). A fallback of `100` therefore yields a column 100× the content width whenever an entry is missing or non-numeric (a truncated or hostile payload, or a row that has more cells than the payload has widths). The correct default is `1 / cols`.

verdict.reason: The quoted line is present verbatim at packages/docs/src/view/clipboard.ts:268, and the unit mismatch is real. `columnWidths` is a ratio in every other producer/consumer: createTableBlock fills `1 / cols` (model/types.ts:542), the DOCX importer divides by totalWidth (import/docx-importer.ts:277), column insert/delete renormalize to `1 / count` (model/document.ts:668, 703), and computeTableLayout multiplies by contentWidth (view/table-layout.ts:140). A fallback of `100` therefore yields a column 100x the content width, and columnXOffsets (table-layout.ts:143-148) accumulate from it, pushing all following columns off-canvas. The fallback is reachable: `rawWidths` defaults to `[]` when `columnWidths` is missing or not an array (clipboard.ts:266), `cols` is derived from the widest row's cell count (clipboard.ts:265), and asNumber rejects any non-finite value (clipboard.ts:69-71), so a missing/short/non-numeric widths array triggers it. The path is live from handlePaste (view/text-editor.ts:1240-1254) through deserializeClipboard (clipboard.ts:347-354) into sanitizeBlock's table branch (clipboard.ts:293), and the payload is explicitly documented as untrusted (clipboard.ts:36-43). I found no clamp or renormalization downstream: insertBlocks only reassigns ids (text-editor.ts:3559-3584) and normalizeTableMerges (model/types.ts:574) only fixes spans. Sibling sanitizers in the same file use DEFAULT_* constants (clipboard.ts:208-210), reinforcing that the bare 100 is an error rather than an intentional unit. No refutation ground applies.
